thread:
sarah: Hey team — hitting an ImportError when importing the Python SDK inside our Docker image after installing via poetry. Works locally in a venv but in Docker we get ModuleNotFoundError: 'redwood.sdk'.

sarah: Repro steps: `poetry build` -> COPY wheel into container -> `pip install /dist/redwood-0.9.7-py3-none-any.whl --no-deps` -> `python -c \"import redwood; print(redwood.__version__)\"` -> raises.

emma: ack, sorry about that. Can you paste `python -c 'import sys; print(sys.path)'` output from the container and the top of the traceback? Also which Python/Poetry versions? :eyeglasses:

sarah: Python 3.11.4, Poetry 1.5.13. Traceback (top):
```
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'redwood.sdk'
  File \"/usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages/redwood/__init__.py\", line 1, in <module>
    from .sdk import client
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'redwood.sdk'
```

sys.path from container: `['', '/usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages', '/usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages/redwood-0.9.7.dist-info']`

raj: hmmm that sys.path looks weird — site-packages contains the .dist-info but not the package dir. Does the wheel actually contain the `redwood` top-level package directory? Can you run `unzip -l /dist/redwood-0.9.7-py3-none-any.whl | sed -n '1,80p'` and paste first 20 lines?

sarah: pasted output snippet:
```
Archive:  /dist/redwood-0.9.7-py3-none-any.whl
  Length      Date    Time    Name
---------  ---------- -----   ----
      123  2025-11-01 12:00   redwood/__init__.py
      890  2025-11-01 12:00   redwood/sdk.py
     2048  2025-11-01 12:00   redwood-0.9.7.dist-info/METADATA
```

miguel: so the wheel has the files. Another guess: some postinstall script or a packaging hook that writes a .pth or sitecustomize which alters import order. Docker-based installs sometimes run extra post-install hooks (e.g., userland scripts in our CI). Can you `ls /usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages` in the container and show any .pth or sitecustomize files?

sarah: `ls` shows: `easy-install.pth  redwood-0.9.7.dist-info  redwood.pth`

emma: there it is — `redwood.pth`. What's inside it?

sarah: `cat /usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages/redwood.pth` -> `/opt/builds/redwood/pkg`

raj: aha. That .pth points at an absolute path from the builder (`/opt/builds/redwood/pkg`) which doesn't exist in the runtime container. When a .pth name matches a top-level package name (`redwood.pth`) it can shadow the installed wheel directory ordering, causing import to look at that path first and then fail. In your venv you may have that path existing (local dev env), so it works.

miguel: To confirm: the import system will process .pth files and add those paths to sys.path early, so a missing directory can effectively cause the package import to fail if the package metadata doesn't register correctly. Could you try removing/renaming `redwood.pth` in the container and then `python -c \"import redwood; print(redwood.sdk.__name__)\"`?

sarah: removed it, re-ran, import now succeeds and prints `redwood.sdk`. So that seems to be it. :tada:

emma: thanks for confirming. Root cause seems to be a packaging/postinstall hook in your build pipeline that emits a `redwood.pth` with an absolute path. We have seen this before with older builder scripts that write `.pth` to help dev installs. Two options: 1) Fix the build to not include that .pth in the wheel (preferred), 2) Make the .pth relative (not recommended), 3) Add cleanup step in Dockerfile to remove any stray `*.pth` matching package names after pip install.

raj: I'm opening an internal issue to add a check in our wheel CI to fail if any `*.pth` is included in the wheel root or site-packages payload (PR referenced). For your immediate unblock, Emma suggested the Dockerfile cleanup step. Example Dockerfile line: `RUN find /usr/local/lib/python*/site-packages -name 'redwood*.pth' -delete`

deploy-bot: build #432 published redwood-0.9.8 (wheel regenerated without stray .pth) :rocket:

sarah: installed 0.9.8 from CI — imports OK in Docker now. Thanks everyone for the fast triage!

emma: Glad it's resolved. We'll push the CI packaging guard to prevent regression. If you can share your build pipeline steps we can add a short note to docs about potential .pth pitfalls with Poetry/legacy postinstall scripts.

sarah: will send pipeline snippet to support@redwood in case you want it. Thanks again! :heart:
